**DEFECT 1: EXPAND mode uses constrained cached size instead of unconstrained size**  
File: `src/draw/lv_draw_label.c`, line 218 (hunk `@@ -218,10 +218,7 @@`)  
The EXPAND path now reads `dsc->text_size.x` which was computed in `lv_label_refr_text` with `max_w` (the object's constrained width). EXPAND mode explicitly requires the *unconstrained* text width (what the text would render at without width limits). The old code correctly passed `LV_COORD_MAX` to `lv_text_get_size`. Result: when a label's text is wider than the object, EXPAND mode will incorrectly use the clamped width, causing incorrect layout/clipping.

**DEFECT 2: Scroll activation uses constrained cached size, preventing scroll**  
File: `src/widgets/label/lv_label.c`, line 852 (hunk `@@ -852,9 +853,7 @@`) and line 892 (hunk `@@ -892,9 +891,7 @@`)  
Both scroll-mode checks compare `size.x > lv_area_get_width(&txt_coords)` using `label->text_size` (computed with `max_w` = object width). Since `lv_text_get_size` clamps the result to `max_w`, `size.x` can never exceed the object width — the condition is never true, so scrolling never activates for overflowing text.

**DEFECT 3: `invalid_size_cache` flag added but never checked**  
File: `src/widgets/label/lv_label_private.h`, line 50 (hunk `@@ -50,6 +50,8 @@`)  
The `invalid_size_cache` bitfield is added to `_lv_label_t` but no code in this diff reads or acts on it. If any label property affecting text size (font, letter_space, line_space, text content) changes without `lv_label_refr_text` being called, the cached `text_size` becomes stale with no invalidation mechanism.

**DEFECT 4: `lv_draw_label_dsc_t.text_size` may be uninitialized**  
File: `src/draw/lv_draw_label.h`, line 35 (hunk `@@ -35,6 +35,9 @@`)  
The new `text_size` field in `lv_draw_label_dsc_t` is only set in `lv_label.c:827`. Other callers of the label draw pipeline (if any) that populate `lv_draw_label_dsc_t` directly will leave `text_size` uninitialized, leading to undefined behavior when `lv_draw_label_iterate_characters` reads it.
